name: The Afscheiding (Secession of 1834)
summary: The secession of orthodox Calvinists, led by Hendrik de Cock, from the state-controlled Dutch Reformed Church, whose members were fined, quartered with soldiers, and jailed, and many of whom emigrated to America.
place: Ulrum, Groningen, and across the Netherlands

start.label: Hendrik de Cock's congregation at Ulrum signs the Act of Secession or Return

end.label: Seceders led by Van Raalte and Scholte emigrate to Michigan and Iowa

background.text: In 1816 King William I reorganized the national church under state-appointed boards; orthodox critics complained of tolerated liberal preaching and of new hymns replacing the Psalms.
Hendrik de Cock, minister at Ulrum, was suspended in 1833 for attacking liberal colleagues and baptizing children from other parishes, and deposed in 1834.

happened.text: De Cock's congregation declared its secession and 'return' to the Reformed confessions in October 1834; other ministers, including Hendrik Scholte, Simon van Velzen, Anthony Brummelkamp, and Albertus van Raalte, joined the movement.
The government treated the seceders' meetings as illegal under a law forbidding gatherings of more than 20 people without permission.
The seceders were granted conditional toleration from 1839–40 under King William II, and formed what became the Christian Reformed Church in the Netherlands.

participants.name: Hendrik de Cock
participants.role: Minister at Ulrum who led the secession

participants.name: Hendrik Scholte
participants.role: Seceder minister who founded Pella, Iowa

participants.name: Albertus van Raalte
participants.role: Seceder minister who founded Holland, Michigan

participants.name: William I
participants.role: King whose government suppressed the seceders

outcomes.text: Thousands of seceders emigrated to the American Midwest, founding Dutch Reformed communities in Michigan and Iowa.
Most seceder churches united with Kuyper's Doleantie churches in 1892; a minority continued as the Christian Reformed Churches in the Netherlands.

condemnations.by: Classis and provincial church board of Groningen
condemnations.reason: Hendrik de Cock deposed from the ministry

persecution.title: Fines, quartering, and imprisonment of the seceders
persecution.summary: Authorities broke up seceder services, fined leaders and hosts heavily, and quartered soldiers in their homes; De Cock was imprisoned for three months in 1835, and other ministers were jailed or fined repeatedly.
persecution.outcome: Toleration from 1839–40; emigration followed in the 1840s.

sources.citation: J. C. H. Blom and E. Lamberts (eds.), History of the Low Countries. New York: Berghahn Books, 1999.
